newsitem.title: UK: UK Conservative leadership seen as six-horse race.
newsitem.headline: UK Conservative leadership seen as six-horse race.

text.p: The struggle for the leadership of Britain's defeated Conservative Party was expected to turn into a six-horse race on Wednesday.
Former Welsh secretary William Hague is scheduled to hold a news conference at 0830 GMT at which he is expected to declare he will stand.
Former health secretary Stephen Dorrell is also expected to throw his hat into the ring on Wednesday.

So far, former finance minister Kenneth Clarke, former social security secretary Peter Lilley, former interior minister Michael Howard and arch-anti-European John Redwood have put themselves forward to succeed John Major.
Major announced he was stepping down last Friday, the morning after Tony Blair's Labour Party dealt the Conservatives their worst election defeat since 1832.

Hague, 36, has become the bookmakers' favourite since former deputy prime minister Michael Heseltine threw the race wide open by deciding he would not stand after he was admitted to hospital at the weekend due to a heart scare.
Whoever emerges as winner faces the formidable task of reuniting a Conservative Party reduced to half its size in the House of Commons by the Labour election landslide.
